run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested 'custom-crd' runbook does not exist for this target (fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND; the only approved runbook is 'service-troubleshooting', which covers service connectivity and not CRD/operator reconciliation), so I carried out the CRD/operator checks with my own tools. In namespace app-96 the CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, v1, Namespaced) is Established=True and NamesAccepted=True, so the API accepts the kind; the operator workload Deployment whale-operator is 1/1 ready and its pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-r2zx4 is Running with restartCount 0, so a crashed or pending operator is not the explanation. The concrete configuration fault found is in RBAC: ClusterRole whale-operator grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers - no update, patch or create, and no whalewatchers/status rule - and it is the only ClusterRole mentioning whalewatchers; it is bound to ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator by ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator, and there is no Role/RoleBinding in app-96 that could add verbs. The v1 CRD declares no subresources and its schema carries status fields lastSeen, observationCount and phase, so any attempt by the operator to record reconciliation on a WhaleWatcher (status write) must be an update/patch of ocean.io whalewatchers, which this ClusterRole does not permit. That is the leading hypothesis (verified configuration, unverified 403): the operator's own container logs returned zero lines at both reads, so no runtime error, 403 or reconcile loop output was observed, and the operator code lives in Secret whale-operator, which cannot be read. Counter-considerations: the whole stack (namespace objects, CRD, ClusterRole/Binding, Deployment, ReplicaSet, pod) was created at 2026-11-23T16:49:11-16:49:13Z, under a minute before the evidence reads at 16:49:53-16:51:04Z, so part of the 'not reconciled' state may simply be a freshly created stack; and the only 6 events in the whole authorized window are Normal rollout events for the whale-operator deployment, with none mentioning a WhaleWatcher, Forbidden, or FailedCreate. Pod status, ServiceAccount presence, absence of NetworkPolicies, absence of ResourceQuotas and absence of any operator ConfigMap were checked and yielded no alternative cause; Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so metrics/traces about the operator are unknown, and the WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves cannot be read with the available tool kinds.

claims.text: The CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io in group ocean.io with version v1, scope Namespaced, exists with conditions NamesAccepted=True and Established=True (lastTransitionTime 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z, reason InitialNamesAccepted).

The v1 version of whalewatchers.ocean.io is served and storage with no conversion (strategy None) and declares no subresources (subresources null); its openAPIV3Schema has no required fields and defines status properties lastSeen, observationCount and phase.

ClusterRole whale-operator contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"] - no update, patch, create or delete verb and no whalewatchers/status resource entry; it was created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z by kubectl-client-side-apply.
ClusterRole whale-operator is the only ClusterRole whose rules mention whalewatchers anywhere in the cluster (84 ClusterRoles scanned).
ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator (created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z) binds ClusterRole whale-operator to subject ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96.
ServiceAccount whale-operator exists in namespace app-96 (created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z) alongside the default ServiceAccount.

No Role or RoleBinding exists in namespace app-96: the Role list returned 12 Roles (kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage only) and the RoleBinding list returned 13 RoleBindings (kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage only), so ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator is the operator ServiceAccount's only observed grant in app-96.

No additional ClusterRoleBinding targets the whale-operator ServiceAccount or service-account groups of app-96: the only bindings whose subjects match app-96 or system:serviceaccounts are system:cluster-trust-bundle-discovery and system:service-issuer-discovery.

Deployment whale-operator in app-96 has 1 replica, 1 available and 1 ready; its container operator uses image python:3.9-slim with command ["python","/app/operator.py"], serviceAccountName whale-operator, env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE taken from fieldRef metadata.namespace, and mounts volume operator-code (secretName whale-operator) at /app; the Deployment was created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z with deployment revision annotation "1".

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-r2zx4 (owner ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66, node opspilot-m1-control-plane) is phase Running, its operator container ready=true with restartCount 0, state running startedAt 2026-11-23T16:49:13Z and an empty lastState.

The only ReplicaSet in app-96 is whale-operator-5f695b7c66, created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z with label pod-template-hash 5f695b7c66, i.e. there is no earlier template revision of the deployment in the cluster.

Cluster-wide there is exactly one Deployment matching whale|operator: app-96/whale-operator (1 replica, 1 ready, image python:3.9-slim, command python /app/operator.py, created 2026-11-23T16:49:12Z), out of 25 Deployments.

The only events returned for the whole authorized window are 6 Normal events, all in namespace app-96 with timestamps 2026-11-23T16:49:12-16:49:13Z: Deployment whale-operator ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-r2zx4 Scheduled, Pulled, Created and Started; no event involves a WhaleWatcher object and no event has a Forbidden or FailedCreate reason.
No NetworkPolicy exists anywhere in the cluster (0 items) and no ResourceQuota exists anywhere in the cluster (0 items).

The 21 ConfigMaps in the cluster include none belonging to the whale operator; in app-96 the only ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt, and no ConfigMap holds operator/watch settings or any fault, delay or error-injection setting.

Leading cause of the missing reconciliation: because ClusterRole whale-operator allows only get/list/watch and the v1 CRD has no status subresource, the operator cannot write reconciliation results (status.phase, status.observationCount, status.lastSeen) back to WhaleWatcher objects - any such write is an update/patch of ocean.io whalewatchers, which the bound ClusterRole does not grant, so writes would be rejected as forbidden and the CRs would never show reconciliation. Missing verbs: update, patch (and whalewatchers/status if a subresource is added).

Alternative cause that could not be excluded: the operator's code is supplied from Secret whale-operator at /app/operator.py and cannot be read, so it is unknown whether it watches ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers in the namespace from OPERATOR_NAMESPACE, uses in-cluster config, or fails at runtime; the operator emitted no log lines in either read, so there is no runtime evidence either way.

Alternative explanation for part of the observed state: the namespace objects, CRD, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Deployment, ReplicaSet and pod were all created at 2026-11-23T16:49:11-16:49:13Z, i.e. less than a minute before the evidence reads (16:49:53-16:51:04Z), so a freshly created stack that had not yet completed a reconcile pass cannot be ruled out as a contributor to 'not reconciled'.

Operator-process failure is not supported by workload state: Deployment whale-operator is 1/1 ready and pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-r2zx4 is Running with restartCount 0 and no container last-termination state, so no crash loop, OOMKilled or restart is observed.
Rejected: a network policy or quota blocking the operator's calls to the API server or its creation of objects. The cluster has no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota objects at all.

Rejected: a restart or rollout of the operator with an unchanged pod template being the trigger. The deployment carries revision "1", there is a single ReplicaSet created in the same second as the deployment, the pod's restartCount is 0 and its container has no previous instance, so no rollout/restart of an existing operator is observed.

Rejected: a missing ServiceAccount or a namespace mismatch of the operator identity. ServiceAccount whale-operator exists in app-96 and is the serviceAccountName of the running pod, and the ClusterRoleBinding subject is ServiceAccount whale-operator in the same namespace app-96.

Grant the whale-operator ServiceAccount the write verbs its reconcile loop needs: update and patch on ocean.io whalewatchers (and whalewatchers/status if a status subresource is added to the CRD), then confirm with an authorization check such as 'kubectl auth can-i update whalewatchers.ocean.io -n app-96 --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator' instead of assuming the ClusterRole is sufficient.

Read the operator's own output next, since it is the missing link: 'kubectl logs -n app-96 deploy/whale-operator' (the earlier reads returned zero lines) and inspect the content of Secret whale-operator's operator.py for the watched group/version/resource and namespace, plus API-server audit logs for 403 responses from system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator.

As an advisory runbook substitute (the requested custom-crd runbook is not available for this target): check (1) CRD served/storage version and Established condition, (2) the controller workload's readiness and its own logs, (3) the controller ServiceAccount's effective RBAC for the CRD group/resource and status subresource, (4) events for the CRs and for Forbidden/FailedCreate reasons, and (5) network policies, quotas and API-server egress - steps 1, 2 (status only), 3, 4 and 5 were carried out here with the results above; the log step produced no lines.

gaps: The requested 'custom-crd' runbook does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND (status error, not citable) and listed only 'service-troubleshooting', which describes service connectivity rather than CRD/operator reconciliation, so no runbook procedure was followed.

The WhaleWatcher custom resources in app-96 could not be read: the Kubernetes tools accept only the fixed built-in kind list and reject custom resources, so the CRs' existence, count, spec, status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen values and any stuck finalizers are unknown.

Operator runtime evidence is missing: fetch_pod_logs for pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-r2zx4 in app-96 returned 0 lines in both reads (16:49:59Z and 16:50:27Z, read window 2026-11-23T15:49:50-16:49:50Z) and no previous container instance existed, so no 403/Forbidden message, no reconcile-log line and no traceback was observed; an empty log read is not proof that nothing happened.

The operator's code and arguments cannot be verified: operator.py is mounted from Secret whale-operator, and secrets cannot be read, so the watched apiVersion/kind/namespace and client configuration are unknown.

Prometheus and Jaeger are unreachable in this Run (get_metric_names returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE twice; traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so controller/reconcile metrics such as kube-state-metrics series and any operator error counters, plus traces, are unknown - not zero.

No change-history source is integrated (change_history is not_integrated), so the ordering of the RBAC write, CRD creation and WhaleWatcher creation cannot be compared and no audit trail of 403 responses is available.

Events only cover 2026-11-23T16:49:12-16:49:13Z (6 Normal events); anything earlier in the 30-day authorized window that could have shown the operator failing is expired or was never recorded, so it is unknown.

Whether a 403 Forbidden was actually returned to the operator, and whether the operator's reconcile loop attempts a status write at all, is unverified - the RBAC gap is a confirmed configuration fact, but the resulting failure is a hypothesis.
next_steps: Run 'kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96' to confirm the effective verbs on ocean.io whalewatchers and whalewatchers/status.

Run 'kubectl logs -n app-96 deploy/whale-operator --tail=200' (and with --previous) to capture the operator's errors, and check API-server audit logs for 403s from system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator.
Inspect the operator code in Secret whale-operator (operator.py) to confirm it watches ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers in app-96 and uses in-cluster config.
Run 'kubectl get whalewatchers.ocean.io -n app-96 -o yaml' to capture the CRs' current status fields and any stale finalizers, which this Run could not read.
Consider adding update/patch on ocean.io whalewatchers and a status subresource to the CRD so reconciliation results can be persisted, before concluding the operator logic itself is wrong.
